ROOT-CAUSED the warp-shuffle libnvvm crash. Bisected with a standalone NVVM harness (scratch/nvvm-probe feeds hand-written IR to libnvvm via the in-tree nvvm crate). FINDING: CUDA 13.3 libnvvm (compute_100/modern dialect) SIGSEGVs while lowering an llvm.nvvm.shfl.sync.* intrinsic that sits in a NON-INLINED callee function. Same intrinsic inlined directly into the kernel entry compiles fine (return type irrelevant). ironsand's shuffle routed through the __nvvm_warp_shuffle wrapper in libintrinsics.ll = exactly such a callee. NVVM lowers shfl BEFORE its inliner, so alwaysinline alone doesn't help; the wrapper must be inlined+DCE'd before the module reaches NVVM. FIX shipped: reimplemented cuda_std::warp::warp_shuffle_32 with inline PTX asm! (shfl.sync.{idx,up,down,bfly}.b32 d|p,...) so it inlines into the kernel and never forms a standalone shfl callee. Fixes all width variants (8/16/64/128 funnel through _32). Verified: gemv_warp compiles + runs correct + ~588 GB/s on lm_head (beats cuBLAS 508).

decision_title: Fix warp shuffle via inline PTX asm! in cuda_std, not the libintrinsics wrapper
decision_reason: libnvvm CUDA 13.3 segfaults lowering shfl.sync in a non-inlined callee (the __nvvm_warp_shuffle libintrinsics wrapper). Inline asm! in warp_shuffle_32 keeps the shuffle inside the kernel where it lowers cleanly, fixing all shuffle width variants. Supersedes the tactical shared-mem-only workaround.

summary: f16 GEMV iteration (exp/gemv-f16). Added gemv_f16_warp (scalar u16 loads) + gemv_f16_vec4 (vectorized 64-bit = 4 f16/load), hardware cvt.f32.f16 via inline asm (reg16->reg32, needs #![feature(asm_experimental_arch)] in kernels crate), f32 accumulate, warp-shuffle reduce (the now-fixed path). RESULTS on sm_120: f16 vec4 hits the f16 DRAM roofline (~485-500 GB/s on L2-overflow shapes) = ~2x faster than the f32 path (half the bytes) and TIES/slightly beats cuBLAS f16 hgemm N=1 (e.g. 32000x4096: vec4 0.524ms/500 vs cuBLAS-f16 0.534ms/491). BONUS: cublasHgemm accumulates in f16 -> lossy (0.15-0.27 rel err); our f32-accumulate is accurate at the same speed. Scalar f16 warp only ~290 GB/s -> vectorized loads essential. Pieces de-risked: f16 compiles via codegen; hardware cvt.f32.f16 asm works (no float reg class, use reg32).

int8 quantized GEMV iteration (exp/gemv-int8) — most zorro-relevant. Two kernels: gemv_i8_warp (W8A32: int8 weights per-row symmetric scale + f32 acts, dequant-in-register) and gemv_i8_dp4a (W8A8: int8 weights x int8 acts via dp4a.s32.s32 4-way int8 dot + i32 accum — GPU analog of zorro's CPU int8 GEMV). Vectorized 32-bit loads (4 int8/load). RESULTS sm_120: i8 dp4a ~4x faster than cuBLAS f32 N=1, ~2x f16, at int8 DRAM roofline (~490-500 GB/s), ALL CORRECT (f32/i32 accumulate keeps accuracy). 32000x4096 lm_head: f32 1.04ms -> f16 0.53ms -> int8 0.27ms. Textbook bandwidth-bound scaling: precision halving = latency halving (4/2/1 bytes). dp4a slightly beats W8A32 (471 vs 434 GB/s). Validates zorro quant strategy + Rust kernels achieve it. dp4a via inline asm (reg32). NEXT toward zorro: sub-byte (Q4_K 4-bit, i2_s ternary 2-bit) = the real zorro decode formats.

ternary i2_s GEMV iteration (exp/gemv-ternary) — zorro's BitNet decode format. gemv_ternary_warp: ternary weights {-1,0,1} as 2-bit codes (w+1) packed 16/u32, int8 acts, i32 sign-accumulate (GPU analog of zorro's _mm256_sign_epi8). RESULTS sm_120: ~7.8x faster than cuBLAS f32 N=1, ~2x faster than int8 dp4a, ALL CORRECT (32000x4096: 0.133ms vs int8 0.266 vs f32 1.04). KEY FINDING: ternary is COMPUTE-BOUND, not memory-bound — only ~240 GB/s effective (~half the ~500 DRAM roofline); at 2 bits/weight (0.25 B) it SHOULD be ~4x int8 if BW-bound but is only 2x. The scalar 16-iter 2-bit unpack loop is the ALU bottleneck — EXACTLY why zorro needed SIMD sign tricks on CPU. NEXT: vectorized/branchless unpack (2-bit→int8 packed + dp4a, or LUT) to push toward roofline = potential another ~2x. GEMV ladder complete: f32(505)→f16(495)→int8(495, all roofline)→ternary(240, compute-bound).

decision_title: Ternary GEMV bottleneck is ALU (2-bit unpack), not memory bandwidth
decision_reason: gemv_ternary_warp hits only ~240 GB/s vs the ~500 DRAM roofline the f32/f16/int8 kernels reach; 2x (not the bandwidth-implied 4x) over int8. The scalar per-code unpack+sign-accumulate loop is compute-bound. Matches zorro's CPU experience (needed _mm256_sign_epi8). Optimization target = vectorized unpack (dp4a or LUT).
summary: Decision: Ternary GEMV bottleneck is ALU (2-bit unpack), not memory bandwidth

OPTIMIZED ternary GEMV (exp/gemv-ternary-opt): gemv_ternary_dp4a removes the scalar-unpack ALU bottleneck. Technique: branchless 2-bit spread (mask/shift/or, keep codes {0,1,2}) -> dp4a int8 dot, with the -1 deferred to a single Σx correction (Σ(c-1)x = Σcx - Σx; x_sum host scalar, same all rows). 4 dp4a/u32 replace 16 scalar imads. RESULT sm_120: ~3.5x faster than scalar ternary (32000x4096: 0.040ms/822 GB/s vs scalar 0.140ms/235; 11008: 0.015/737 vs 0.047/239). ALU-bound -> memory/L2-bound, correctness preserved. This is the GPU analog of zorro's _mm256_sign_epi8 SIMD sign trick. Resolves the earlier 'ternary is ALU-bound' tactical decision. (Bench note: laptop GPU thermally throttles over the long 11-kernel-per-shape run; trust adjacent-kernel relative speedups, not cross-run absolutes.)

Q4_K GEMV iteration (exp/gemv-q4k) — GGUF 4-bit k-quant, zorro's other decode format. gemv_q4k_warp: byte-faithful block_q4_K (256-weight super-blocks, f16 d/dmin, 8×6-bit sub-scales+mins packed in 12B via get_scale_min_k4, 128B of 4-bit qs low/high nibble), affine dequant w=d*sc*q-dmin*mn. Warp-per-row, lane owns weight  of every sub-block (coalesced nibble+act reads, broadcast header). CORRECT on all k%256==0 shapes (4096/11008/12288/32000) — validates the 6-bit scale bit-packing round-trips through get_scale_min_k4 (the trickiest part). Guarded k%256!=0 (e.g. 384) out. PERF: heavily COMPUTE-bound ~97 GB/s (~5× off ~500 roofline); 32000x4096 Q4_K 0.758ms vs int8 0.361 vs tern-dp4a 0.040 — slower than int8 despite fewer bytes. Bottleneck = affine dequant + per-sub-block 6-bit unpack done 32× redundantly by all lanes. NEXT OPT: decode header once via lane0+shuffle broadcast, nibble→int8 + dp4a, precompute d_eff/m_eff per sub-block. CAVEAT: validated self-consistent (kernel vs my packer through get_scale_min_k4), NOT byte-verified vs a real llama.cpp GGUF tensor — that needs a reference tensor (closed-loop-oracle caveat).

Optimized Q4_K GEMV (exp/gemv-q4k-opt): gemv_q4k_fast = decode super-block d/dmin (f16 cvt) ONCE per 256 weights instead of 8x per sub-block, keeping the coalesced lane=weight inner layout. ~1.3-2.0x faster (2x on L2-resident shapes 187-208 GB/s, 1.3x on 32000x4096 130 GB/s), all correct. JOURNEY/LESSON: first attempt made each lane own whole sub-blocks (to 'amortize the redundant header decode 32x') — REGRESSED 1.6x slower! In SIMT the per-sub-block header decode is ONE instruction-issue (lanes compute identical values in lockstep, not 32x cost), and lane-owns-sub-block scattered the nibble reads, killing coalescing. Coalescing >> header ALU. The REAL redundancy was re-cvt'ing the SAME super-block d/dmin on all 8 sub-blocks. Still ~2-4x off roofline (per-sub-block scale_min + affine fma + low ILP); further: multiple accumulators for ILP, or dp4a-affine with int8 acts (W4A8).

decision_title: Q4_K opt: amortize super-block d/dmin, do NOT restructure lanes off the coalesced layout
decision_reason: Decoding d/dmin once per 256-weight super-block (not per sub-block) gives ~1.3-2x while keeping lane=weight coalesced nibble reads. The alternative (lane owns whole sub-blocks) amortizes more header ALU but scatters memory and runs 1.6x SLOWER — in SIMT the header decode is one issue, coalescing dominates.
summary: Decision: Q4_K opt: amortize super-block d/dmin, do NOT restructure lanes off the coalesced layout

Q6_K decode GEMV (exp/gemv-q6k) — zorro-foreman's named fattest lever (lm_head ~20% of step). gemv_q6k_warp: byte-faithful GGUF block_q6_K (210B: ql128+qh64+scales16 int8+d f16; 16×16-weight sub-blocks; 6-bit q=ql_nibble|qh_2bits, w=d*scale*(q-32)); ql/qh interleaving per llama.cpp dequantize_row_q6_K, lane l∈[0,32) owns weights l,l+32,l+64,l+96 per 128-group (coalesced ql/qh). d factored per super-block. CORRECT all shapes vs f64 ref (intricate interleaving validated). PERF: 255-366 GB/s, FASTER than my Q4_K (Q6_K flat int8 scales avoid Q4_K's 6-bit get_scale_min_k4 unpack). lm_head 32000x4096: 0.42ms (2.4x cuBLAS-f32). NEXT for zorro integration: package as load_ptx module + bench vs gemv_q6k_mmvq in ZORRO_BENCH_ONLY harness; W6A32 here, confirm zorro decode act dtype. Caveat: self-consistent (packer↔kernel), not byte-verified vs real GGUF tensor (asked zorro-foreman for one).

decision_title: Q6_K fast (mul_add FMA + 2-way super-block unroll) gives no speedup over Q6_K warp — ~0% on 4096², slightly slower on the larger shapes
decision_reason: PTX confirms warp already emits 10 fma.rn.f32 (compiler fused MUL+ADD into FMA), and the kernel is memory-bandwidth-bound at ~380 GB/s (≈21% of the 5070 Ti's 1.79 TB/s peak). Doubling FMA count via 2-way unroll just adds instructions that wait on memory; same or slightly worse wall time across all 5 bench shapes.

decision_title: Q4_K v3 (pair-of-sub-blocks + u32 scale reads + FMA) is 1.04-1.13x faster than Q4_K fast across all 5 bench shapes; best +13% on 12288x4096
decision_reason: Three changes on top of fast, all real wins: (1) per-group outer loop reads each qs byte once instead of twice (sub=2g and sub=2g+1 share the byte; compiler likely can't CSE through runtime sub), (2) 3 u32 reads replace ~12 byte reads of the 12-byte scales array, (3) f32::mul_add FMA chains the d·nib − m expression. Q4_K is compute-bound on the affine dequant (2 mults + 1 sub per weight), so reducing instruction count helps even though the kernel isn't memory-bound at 220-270 GB/s.
summary: Decision: Q4_K v3 (pair-of-sub-blocks + u32 scale reads + FMA) is 1.04-1.13x faster than Q4_K fast across all 5 bench shapes; best +13% on 12288x4096

decision_title: Q4_K v4 (2-way super-block unroll on v3) is mixed: +2%/+9% on 4096² and 32000×4096, but -3%/-8%/-9% on the 3 mid-sized shapes
decision_reason: Pattern suggests the 2× per-block live state (sc/mn arrays, d, dmin) tips the lane over the 64-register budget on the mid-sized shapes and nvvm spills to local memory. 32000×4096 has the most super-blocks per row (125 = 62 pairs) so the unroll's ILP wins offset the spill cost; 4096×11008 (43 = 21 pairs) and 12288×4096 (48 = 24 pairs) sit in the bad zone. v3 stays the default; v4 is a documented experiment.

summary: GEMV series plateau reached. Final state: Q4_K v3 is the production Q4_K (224-269 GB/s, +4-13% over fast). Q6_K warp is the production Q6_K (~380 GB/s, ~21% of 5070 Ti peak). gemv_q4k_v4 (2-way unroll) and gemv_q6k_fast (FMA + unroll) are documented no-wins kept in tree as experiments.
